Prevention: Plant as early as possible and use fast-maturing strains of crop so it can be harvested before quelea reaches an area
As soon as quelea appears, protect small plots by banging and and making loud noises to scare them away.
If they have newly built nests or unhatched eggs they may not return
Place several scarecrows in the field
Create physical barriers using materials such as string and streamers
Create an area where quelea can be trapped by planting purpose grown patches of grass which quelea eats, such as napier grass
Harvest small colonies for food, either directly from nests or by catching flying adults
Monitoring: Relevant crops: sorghum, millet, rice, teff, wheat and other small-sized cereals
The birds look drab and have a distinctive red bill.
They are small, between 11-13 cm long when adult, and weigh about 15-20 g
It is sometimes possible to predict when quelea will appear.
They migrate and breed when there is enough rain to stimulate the germination of grass seed - their food source
Direct Control: Assess the risk from quelea attack before committing money and time to control programmes.
Quelea are very difficult to control because of their large populations
Trap birds if population is low.
Use a traditional basket trap made of grass or wire mesh, a mist net, or a roost trap
